sentences.text:
This is first bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C filed on behalf of applicant for grant of bail,
pending the trial.

The applicant is in custody since 20.09.2022 in connection with Crime No.546/2022, registered at P.S.-Madhotal, District Jabalpur (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 363,366,376(2)(n) and 506 of IPC and Section 5L/6 of POCSO Act, 2012.
As per the prosecution story on 09.09.2022, prosecutrix's father lodged a report that her 17 year and 3 months old daughter is missing from home since 09.09.2022.
F.I.R was registered under section 363 of IPC.
On 17.09.2022 prosecutrix was medically examined and her vaginal swab was sent for examination and on it human sperms are detected.

As per medical report and prosecutrix's statement under section 164 of Cr.P.C, on 12.09.2022, applicant had committed rape/ aggravated Rajendra @ Chhotu Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94388822/
1 penetrative sexual assault upon her.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has falsely been implicated.
It is submitted that applicant was having love affair with the prosecutrix.
Prosecutrix on her own had gone with the applicant.
Applicant has not committed any rape/ aggravated penetrative sexual assault upon her.

Learned counsel for the applicant has contended that it is the specific version of the prosecutrix that rape was committed upon her on 12.09.2022, whereas, prosecutrix was medically examined on 17.09.2022 almost after five days of the incident.
After five days of the incident, presence of human sperms on the vaginal swab of the prosecutrix makes the prosecution story doubtful.
Therefore, it has been prayed that applicant may be released on bail.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the grant of bail to the applicant.
As per prosecutrix, she had gone with the applicant on her own.

Taking into consideration the other facts and circumstances of the case including the fact that after investigation charge sheet has been filed and trial of the case would take considerable time, I am of the view that it is a case in which applicant may be released on bail.
Consequently, this first bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

It is directed that applicant - Rajendra @ Chhotu Yadav be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.
He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.
(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE MKL Rajendra @ Chhotu Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94388822/
